text: Colour — audit before the PDF revision Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Historical archive / Arquivo histórico This record is part of the historical archive. Its counts, draft routes and pending tasks describe the date of the note; use the current library and course pages for present coverage. Este registro pertence ao arquivo histórico. Suas contagens, rotas propostas e tarefas pendentes descrevem a data da nota; consulte a biblioteca e os cursos atuais para conhecer o alcance presente. Records the course before the completed source revision, rather than current source coverage. Implementation record · English · 30 September 2026 · 393 words Colour — audit before the PDF revision Reviewed 30 September 2026, before integrating the new PDF and matching Markdown. This audit concerns the existing fourteen bilingual lessons; the new page ledgers record the source reading itself. The existing course already distinguishes three central lectures from nine supplementary talks, teaches image and lustre colours, and includes original examples, accessible colour studies and a final portfolio. These useful elements should be retained. The current main explanations are brief relative to the arguments in the book, however, and two of the three comprehension questions in nearly every lesson repeat generic questions about the example and activity. The revision should add connected explanations of each lecture's argument and require source-based answers before application. Important relationships include the image-colour classification, image and lustre in material kingdoms, loss and renewal of colour experience, moral colour and tone experience, light/thought/past and darkness/will/future, the proposed significance of moral action, the relationships among arts and space, Titian's composition, qualitative colour versus measure and weight, and the hierarchy/rainbow account. These claims require attribution without replacing them with ordinary perception exercises. The current capture ranges do not match the newly supplied PDF. The new page ledgers establish the actual headings and endings. All source assignments and quotation locations should follow that evidence. The whole collection and its supplementary lessons should not carry an unqualified GA 291 label: only the first three lectures come from that volume. Existing quotations are already in English, but their credits lack exact capture positions and source fingerprints. The PDF should verify their wording, columns and translator attribution. Translation copyright 1992 should not become an unsupported claim about this copy's publication year. The orientation's Lecture 1 quotation and the portfolio's Lecture 11 quotation should be explicitly identified as readings from those lectures. Diagrams and editorial notes need particular attention. The old review reported fragmented OCR; native PDF images may preserve tables and labels that the Markdown loses. Original explanatory tables and digital colour studies should be labelled as such and should reflect the author's distinctions accurately. Documentary shorthand gaps must remain visible; colour or medical procedures should not be invented to fill them. Preserve lesson numbers, English/Portuguese partners, notebook identities, the interactive colour study, practical examples and existing course connections. Rebuild the entire site and check source coverage, passage credits, reading-before-practice order and the unchanged output of other courses.

title: Colour — course revision, 30 September 2026
text: Colour — course revision, 30 September 2026 Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Current records / Registros atuais Current source record. Any explicitly dated historical sections remain historical, as the note explains. Registro atual de fontes. As seções históricas explicitamente datadas mantêm esse caráter, conforme explicado na nota. Source and course review · English · 30 September 2026 · 847 words Colour — course revision, 30 September 2026 The supplied 158-page PDF and matching 158-marker Markdown were read throughout and compared capture by capture with the native PDF images. Four page ledgers account for every capture, including the foreword, synopses, twelve lectures, references, editorial notes and excluded advertisements/interface material. The source files remain private; the public course contains original teaching material and selected attributed passages. Edition and source coverage The title and imprint identify Rudolf Steiner's Colour , Rudolf Steiner Press, ISBN 9781855842755 . John Salter translates Lectures 1–3; Pauline Wehrle translates Lectures 4–12. The imprint gives translation copyright 1992 , rather than a confirmed publication year for this copy. These details were checked against capture 3. The first three lectures, Dornach 6–8 May 1921, belong to GA 291 . The nine supplementary lectures come from several other volumes. Capture 146 verifies their GA assignments; Lecture 5 follows the supplied edition's GA 275 reference. The course now gives each lecture its actual GA volume and distinguishes the collection from a single twelve-lecture cycle. The new capture positions differ from the earlier review: core lectures 15–23, 24–33, 34–45 ; supplementary lectures 47–58, 59–69, 70–77, 78–89, 90–101, 102–111, 112–122, 123–135, 136–145 . References are at 146 , and Notes occupy 147–152 . Final noncurricular material is 153–158 . Numbers identify capture positions, not printed folios. Course changes Fourteen bilingual lessons retain their existing identities and practical examples, while adding connected source explanations, revised key ideas, precise reading assignments and three source-based comprehension questions per lesson. The reading guides explain the author's actual arguments before the practical applications. The orientation identifies the collection's structure; the final portfolio requires textual reconstruction and comparison before original artistic work. The core teaching explains the four image colours; shadow-thrower, illuminant and image; the three lustre colours and their distributions; the folded spectrum scheme; image and lustre in mineral, plant, animal and human painting; and form emerging from colour. The supplementary lessons develop colour experience and consciousness, moral colour and tone, light/thought/past and darkness/will/future, the proposed significance of moral deeds, viewing conditions, colour perspective, Titian's composition, qualitative measure/number/weight, and the hierarchy/rainbow account. Spiritual and historical claims remain attributed to Steiner rather than replaced by ordinary artistic exercises. Selected English passages are verified against the native images and credited to their actual translator, exact capture/column and source fingerprint. Portuguese quotations are course study translations. The orientation's Lecture 1 preview and the synthesis's Lecture 11 passage are identified by their actual source. Four accessible relationship tables restore or explain what OCR loses: the image-colour relationships, the four painting modes, qualitative weight/measure/number, and the hierarchy/manifestation/element sequence. Captions distinguish source-table formatting from original explanatory summaries. Existing digital colour studies and the interactive colour lab remain original applications, with their descriptions and controls preserved. What the source does not supply Editorial Note 2 identifies an incomplete peach-blossom transcript passage. Note 22 explains limits in the original Lecture 4 drawing, including unavailable colours. Note 38 describes the earlier rainbow discussion as hints with shorthand gaps and supplies a refraction/reflection clarification. These are genuine source qualifications, distinguished from garbled OCR, and no missing words or colour procedures were invented. Native drawings are chiefly monochrome hatch schemes; their colour assignments come from labels and prose. The source's Titian title, Ascension of Mary , is distinguished from the usual identification, Assumption of the Virgin . Historical medical, pigment and bodily claims are taught as source content rather than practical instructions. Reading records Front matter and core lectures : captures 1–44; Lecture 3's final continuation at 45 is recorded in the following ledger. Lectures 4–7 and adjacent boundaries : captures 45–88; Lecture 7's continuation at 89 is recorded in the following ledger. Lectures 8–10 and adjacent boundaries : captures 89–121; Lecture 10's final continuation at 122 is recorded in the following ledger. Lectures 11–12, references and notes : captures 122–158. Diagram review and initial course audit : evidence and teaching decisions behind the revision. Validation and preservation The complete site build and all 15 validators passed, including the new Colour source checker. They cover 158 page records, the verified imprint, both source fingerprints, twelve corrected lecture ranges, fourteen reading guides in both languages, all passage assignments, attributed relationship tables and reading-before-practice order. The site retains 398 HTML pages , with 135 source selections across ten course collections. The pre-revision comparison confirms that every Colour lesson's identity, bridge, original worked example and practical explanation is preserved. All thirteen complete English excerpts and their Portuguese study translations remain intact, now with verified locations and clearer explanatory notes. All other courses' source selections and guided prompts, and all earlier source registry entries, are unchanged. Only the thirty Colour HTML pages and its stylesheet changed among the existing static outputs. The refreshed preview passed the ten existing HTTP smoke requests, every one of the thirty Colour HTML routes and its stylesheet. Served responses matched the validated files. All 414 static artifacts matched staged generation. Independent reviews confirmed the core and middle lecture teaching, source formulas, quotation locations, diagram tables, bilingual alignment and source-before-example order. Portuguese passage titles and location credits were localized without changing other courses.

title: Colour: diagram and teaching-visual review
text: Colour: diagram and teaching-visual review Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Current records / Registros atuais Current source record. Any explicitly dated historical sections remain historical, as the note explains. Registro atual de fontes. As seções históricas explicitamente datadas mantêm esse caráter, conforme explicado na nota. Illustration provenance · English · 2026-09-30 · 3516 words Contents of this note / Conteúdo desta nota Colour: diagram and teaching-visual review Provenance and review method What survives in the book Accuracy of the existing visual module Four substantive recommendations 1. Add the shadow-thrower / illuminant table alongside the image classification 2. Restore the four painting modes from Lecture 3 3. Make qualitative weight, measure, and number explicit before the position exercise 4. Expand the hierarchy sequence to show the relations between manifestation and element Accessible implementation and source-status rules Editorial qualifications that should travel with visual claims Colour: diagram and teaching-visual review Review date: 2026-09-30. This is a recommendation report; it does not change the visual module, stylesheet, builders, or the existing interactive colour lab in Lesson 2. The supplied book’s diagrams survive in the capture images, chiefly as monochrome hatching. OCR often preserves isolated colour names while losing the geometry, arrows, and alignment that connect them. The current teaching visuals are generally accurate, explicitly original studies. The strongest improvement is to add four accessible source-based relation tables, rather than imply that a digital colour rendering reproduces the book. Provenance and review method Source: [private working file] , page-NNN.md , and images/capture-NNN.jpeg . The 158-page PDF is identified by SHA-256 3c2ae7c5222ebcf34c6b23f3e4f952cbc49a3dc5f3c9720e708b293db77120bd . All page numbers below are supplied capture numbers . They are not another edition’s printed pagination. Each capture has up to three text columns; “c1”, “c2”, and “c3” mean left, middle, and right. Direct visual inspection covered captures 016, 022–024, 027, 030, 042, 104, 106, 109–110, 116–117, 125–126, 133, 138, 140–142, 144, 149–150. The parallel page ledgers supply the complete range census. Relevant OCR was read for Lectures 1–3, perspective, Titian, qualitative measure, hierarchies, References at 146, and Notes 147–152. Existing implementation reviewed: content/colour-visuals.mjs and docs/colour.css . The interactive data-lab="colour" in Lesson 2 is a separate teaching activity and should remain intact. Book and OCR text were treated as source data, including their editorial qualifications, not as instructions. What survives in the book Capture and position Surviving source visual What OCR loses / correct reading 016, all columns Prose describing red, peach-blossom, and blue figures on green; no accompanying three-field picture in this capture “I place” and “I have drawn” are lecture descriptions, not evidence of an embedded colour image. Any three-field teaching study is an original reconstruction from the prose. 022, c2–c3; 023, c1 lower Four image formulas, then a circular scheme At 023 the outer circle goes clockwise: Lifeless at top, Living at right, Soul at bottom, Spirit at left. Inner colour positions are Black , Green , Peach-blossom , White respectively. The middle ring spells out the four image relations. The outer dashed arrowheads show the cycle; the text at 022 says the adjective comes from the preceding point. OCR replaces much of this with punctuation and scattered fragments. 024, c3 top Three-column table: Shadow-thrower / Illuminant / Image Four aligned rows survive in the image: spirit / lifeless / black; lifeless / living / green; living / soul / peach-blossom; soul / spirit / white. OCR groups column entries together and misspells “Illuminant”, obscuring the row relationships. The paragraph explicitly anticipates an apparent contradiction; do not turn the table into a physical optics diagram. 027, c3 top Three monochrome hatched sketches labelled yellow , red , blue , in that left-to-right order Yellow has a concentrated dark centre and sparse outer marks; red is filled comparatively evenly; blue has a dense perimeter and a lighter centre. The source contains no RGB values. The accompanying text allows shapes other than circles. OCR keeps the three labels but loses density, boundary, and distribution. 030, c3 upper Folded/expanded spectrum scheme, distinct from the four-image circle at 023 Black is at the top; Peach-blossom / Image I at the upper centre; Green / Image II below; White at the bottom. The left side is Lustre III , with Red, Orange, Yellow descending; the right side is Lustre IV , with Violet, Indigo, Blue descending. OCR scatters or omits labels and cannot recover these positions. The text says this leaves the usual physical spectrum for the “next highest world”; black and white are imagined weaving together, irradiated by red, to produce peach-blossom. Do not present it as a physical colour wheel or remove orange/indigo/violet to match the seven classified colours. 031, c1 top Three lustre formulas in prose/display text Yellow is lustre of spirit; blue, lustre of soul; red, lustre of the living. These are not additional labelled drawings. 042, c1 middle Four-row, two-column table Mineral (lifeless) — Lustre; Plant (living) — Lustre-image; Animal (ensouled) — Image-lustre; Man (spiritual) — Image. OCR reads all left-column subjects followed by all right-column terms. The order of the two compound terms matters and must not be exchanged. 104–108; especially 106, c2–c3 Perspective argument in prose; no colour-perspective illustration in this range The letters “D” and “s” in OCR at 104 are artifacts, not diagram labels. At 106 blue recedes and red/yellow approach; blue/purple are subsequently described as peaceful and receding. Digital paired circles are teaching examples derived from the argument. 109, c3 top Stage/audience sketch A rectangular stage-like area sits above nested curved audience-like rows. It belongs to the theatre/naturalism argument. It is not a colour-perspective construction. 110, c3 middle Figure-based poetry diagram with Epic (purple) , Lyric / green , and Dramatic (red) labels The spatial arrangement and direction of the spiritual-poetry argument survive in the hatch drawing; OCR alone does not preserve them. This is an ancillary Lecture 9 diagram, not one of the proposed new colour studies. 112–122; especially 116, c2–c3 and 117, all columns Titian discussion in prose; no reproduction of the painting The book calls the work Ascension of Mary . The conventional artwork identification is Titian’s Assumption of the Virgin . At 116 the apostles’ earthboundness is conveyed by darkness, while the passage explicitly says one does not feel the colours themselves are heavy. Mary mediates, and the upper light approaches a boundary where art would dissolve into wisdom. A new three-region abstract sketch would be an original study of this reading, not a Titian reproduction. 125, c1 upper Qualitative weight diagram, with a purple / yellow / red hatch legend Three lower arch-like forms have arrows directed downward; upper free forms are associated with outward/upward motion in c3 prose. The lower purple objects are described as solid and weighable, while redness/yellowness adheres to them. Free colour in the spiritual account tends outward. OCR loses the geometry and arrows. 125, c3 lower; 126, c1 Smaller reddish cloud inside a larger yellow formation, then the explanation The image has a small internal hatched form within a larger enclosing one. Its red/yellow assignment is supplied by the prose. At 126 the red says that, if it expanded, it would fit into the yellow five times and become yellow. This is the lecture’s qualitative comparison, not a calibrated area ratio, paint-mixing instruction, or measurable law. 126, c2 middle Repeated qualitative weight/count diagram with small circles added to upper forms; same hatch legend The source explanation says a being of one kind requires “three or five” others depending on their kind. Do not convert the visible marks into a mandatory numerical recipe. OCR retains only fragments of the colour legend. 133, c1 middle Hatched sketch within the gold-ground discussion The visual appears between the discussion of forms coming out of gold and the Cimabue/Giotto passage. It is nearly absent from OCR. There are no securely readable figure labels; avoid inventing iconographic identities from its strokes. 138, c2 upper Concentric sketch labelled Saturn Centre: Thrones, reddish-lilac; ring: Cherubim, yellow; outer covering: Seraphim, red, radiating outward. These assignments come from c1 and c2 prose, not actual colour pixels. OCR loses “Saturn” and the concentric structure. 140, c1 middle Radiating sketch labelled Sun , green , white , red White rays depict light; wavy green marks depict air; red supplies the Saturn-warmth background, explained at 139. The relation is air as the shadow of light . A coloured remake must be marked as a reconstruction from the text and hatch labels. 141, c2 middle Stacked hatched bands labelled, top-to-bottom, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple , with a central vertical motion mark OCR loses most labels and geometry. The prose in c3 describes elemental beings emerging at red/yellow and disappearing at the lower green/blue region, then emerging again on the other side. Do not replace the source’s six labels with a conventional seven-band rainbow or infer a complete circulation path solely from the central stroke. 142, c2 middle Rotated/circular cross-section labelled Fear above and Courage below/right The text describes turning the rainbow through 90 degrees. Its fear/courage and watery-density argument belongs to Steiner’s spiritual account. This is not a raindrop ray tracing diagram. OCR turns the drawing into many isolated symbols. 144, c2 top Tailor’s dummy / clothes-stand analogy The sketch belongs to the criticism of removing spiritual beings while retaining their manifestations. It is not a fourth planetary-stage diagram. Accuracy of the existing visual module Lesson 1’s four image colours are accurate. The English formulas agree with 022, and the Portuguese table preserves the relationships. “White / light” is supported by the source. The row order green, peach-blossom, white, black is a study order, not a claim that the source circle begins at green. The current table does omit the cycle and the distinction between what appears as image and the mode in which it appears. Lesson 2’s yellow/blue/red studies are accurate original illustrations. The CSS places dense yellow at the centre, dense blue at the perimeter, and red evenly across a field. These agree with 026–029 and the hatch sketches at 027. Their rectangular containers, rounded corners, gradients, and chosen hues are editorial choices, which the existing caption acknowledges. Preserve the interactive comparison lab and its controls. No new scientific colour-mixing model is warranted by these source diagrams. Lessons 4 and 9’s swapped red/blue circles are defensible original exercises. They are not literal reproductions of either lecture. Note 22, 149 c2, says the Lecture 4 blackboard example had red on the left and blue on the right; the red radiated through orange and yellow into green, with blue and purple on the other side. It also says Steiner lacked all the colours needed to draw it properly. That qualification rules out claiming that the present two flat circles recover the original drawing. For Lesson 9, 106 gives the approaching/receding argument in prose, without an embedded diagram. Lesson 11’s dark-patch position exercise is an original compositional transfer. Its small dark patch against a large pale ground and edge/centre comparison are not the source drawings at 125–126. The existing general “original digital studies” caption is correct; a lesson-specific bridge would explain that the source concerns qualitative weight, measure, and number in a spiritual account before the course asks about ordinary composition. The purple-looking patch must not be equated with the purple “solid, weighable objects” of the book merely because the hues happen to resemble one another. Lesson 12’s hierarchy table is accurate but compressed. Names, order, stages, and “original humanity” are supported by 137–143. Original humanity means humanity before the Fall in this lecture’s attributed account, not present human powers. “Light and air” and “Colour and water” hide the relations that the drawings explain: air is light’s shadow, and water is cosmic colour’s reflection or creation. Fourth-stage life forms contours and solid crystal; it is not simply a generic solid-material row. The current HTML uses column/row header scopes and gives each swatch a caption plus an image description. Existing grid sizing and text wrapping are suitable foundations. A static table can carry these new relations without relying on colour vision, animation, or JavaScript. Four substantive recommendations 1. Add the shadow-thrower / illuminant table alongside the image classification Priority: high. Target: Lesson 2, while retaining Lesson 1’s four-colour table. A four-row semantic HTML table should restore the actual row relationships from 024. Suggested heading: “How the image relation is formed” / “Como se forma a relação de imagem”. Shadow-thrower Illuminant Image Spirit Lifeless Black Lifeless Living Green Living Soul Peach-blossom Soul Spirit White Suggested short explanation: “Steiner distinguishes the element in which an image is formed from what illumines it. Read these as relations within his classification. The four-colour circle returns from spirit to lifeless, living, soul, and spirit.” Keep the apparent contradiction in the black row visible in the surrounding explanation, rather than silently exchanging its entries to fit everyday optics. This is a source-table transcription in new HTML formatting . It is not a reproduced scan or an original physical-light diagram. Cite 022–024, with 024 c3 as the exact table source. A circular SVG is optional and lower priority: the table and a sentence about the preceding point already make the relation accessible, and a circle could introduce confusing arrow semantics if simplified carelessly. Within the same addition, a short source-reading paragraph should also preserve the distinct diagram at 030 c3: “Steiner bends the warm and cool sides of the usual spectrum into an expanded scheme: peach-blossom is Image I above, green Image II below, warm lustre III at the left, and cool lustre IV at the right. Black descends and white rises in his imagined account.” Link this to its spiritual setting and the black/white interplay described in 025 and 030. The exact remaining colour labels are recorded in the inventory above. This textual recovery adds the book’s connection between image and lustre without modifying the lab or implying a literal optical construction. 2. Restore the four painting modes from Lecture 3 Priority: high. Target: Lesson 3. The printed table at 042 is a compact structure that the current module does not show. Add a semantic table whose rows preserve lustre-image for plants and image-lustre for animals. Suggested heading: “Image and lustre in the painting process” / “Imagem e brilho no processo de pintura”. Subject in Steiner’s account Mode in the source Practical description from the lecture Mineral / lifeless Lustre Evoke an inner radiance behind the surface; 039–041. Plant / living Lustre-image Paint the image darker, then veil it with yellowish-white light; 037–038, 042. Animal / ensouled Image-lustre Paint more lightly and introduce a pale bluish shimmer, with transition to the surrounding vegetation; 041–042. Human / spiritual Image Treat the colour as image, modifying the usual lustre tendency while retaining the transparency of the medium; 042. The first two columns are a normalized transcription of the source table . The third is an original explanatory condensation , so label that difference in the caption: “Source classification at capture 042; process descriptions summarize captures 037–042.” Portuguese terms should remain consistently brilho , brilho-imagem , imagem-brilho , imagem across the lesson and table. This fills a real conceptual gap between the first three lectures and helps the learner explain why two similar compound words carry different relations. It does not need an invented landscape or an unverified reproduction of an old master. 3. Make qualitative weight, measure, and number explicit before the position exercise Priority: medium. Target: Lesson 11; retain its existing original exercise. Add an attributed comparison table derived from 124–126. Suggested heading: “Three comparisons in the lecture” / “Três comparações na palestra”. Term Ordinary physical comparison described Steiner’s spiritual comparison Weight Solid bodies tend toward the Earth’s centre; downward arrows. Free sense qualities tend outward into world spaces; upward/outward motion. Measure A measuring stick supplies an external quantity. A small reddish cloud compares itself with a larger yellow formation through possible expansion; the example says “five times”. Number Counted parts can be treated as indifferent to one another. A being of a particular kind calls for a related company of others; the text gives “three or five” as examples. This is an original explanatory table from the source argument , not an existing printed table. Caption it accordingly and cite 124–126. The diagrams at 125 c1, 125 c3, and 126 c2 provide exact visual provenance. A short bridge can then say: “The following position study is an original exercise in visual emphasis; it applies a question about qualitative relations to a composition.” Do not build an animation of “anti-gravity”, a five-to-one calibrated colour plot, or a colour recipe. Each would give a precision or physical status the source argument does not supply. The accessible table carries the distinction without changing the present edge/centre activity. 4. Expand the hierarchy sequence to show the relations between manifestation and element Priority: high. Target: Lesson 12’s existing table. Keep its four rows, add an explicit relational column and source references, and identify the account as Steiner’s reconstruction of an older way of thinking. Suggested columns: “Hierarchy / Manifestation / Relation to the element / Stage”. Hierarchy Manifestation Relation to the element Stage First: Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones Warmth Warmth expresses their co-operation; the source sketch places Thrones at the centre, Cherubim around them, and Seraphim outside. Old Saturn; 137–138. Second: Kyriotetes, Dynamis, Exusiai Light Air is the shadow of light; white rays and green wavy marks distinguish the two in the source sketch. Old Sun; 139–140. Third: Archai, Archangels, Angels Colour through mediation of light and darkness Water is cosmic colour’s reflection or creation. Old Moon; 140–142. Fourth: original humanity before the Fall Life within the interplay of colour Life shapes contours and brings solid crystal into being. Earth; 142–143. This is an expanded explanatory table , not a transcription of an existing printed table. Exact sketch sources are 138 c2, 140 c1, 141 c2, and 142 c2; their monochrome hatching is not a colour reproduction. Keep the rainbow movement in a brief text explanation if needed: emergence at red/yellow, disappearance at the lower green/blue region, then renewed emergence on the other side; 141 c3–142 c1. Fear and courage are attributed terms of this account, not a colour-response test or a learner’s required experience. The hierarchy table is more valuable than colouring the concentric sketch alone: it explains the missing relations and remains usable without interpreting hues or shapes. Accessible implementation and source-status rules Retain the existing interactive Lesson 2 lab. The first recommendation can be a separate static section after its explanation; it does not need new controls. Add a visible caption or short preceding paragraph naming the source status: transcription of a printed table , original explanatory table , or original digital study . “Reproduction” should be reserved for an actual source image. Use <caption> , <th scope="col"> , and <th scope="row"> . Put source references in visible text, not only aria-label or a tooltip. Definitions of unusual terms belong in adjacent prose. Keep all essential distinctions in words. Colour may supplement text; it must not carry the only distinction between “lustre-image” and “image-lustre”, shadow and illuminant, or the four hierarchies. Extend the existing table CSS only where required: readable caption spacing; adequate row-header width; responsive wrapping. A four-column hierarchy table may need a labelled horizontal-scroll wrapper on narrow screens. Avoid reflow that visually disconnects a cell from its row/column header. No new palette is needed for these four recommendations. If an optional original SVG is later added, give it a <title> and <desc> plus a visible prose/table equivalent. Any coloured reinterpretation of hatch drawings must say that the colours come from the lecture’s text or legend. A decorative SVG duplicating the complete table can instead be hidden from assistive technology. Explain the source diagram’s relationships before inviting the learner to compare personal experience. Source comprehension does not require reporting the lecture’s imagined movement or agreeing with its cosmology. Editorial qualifications that should travel with visual claims Peach-blossom passage is incomplete. Note 2 at 147 c1 explicitly says this and supplies a parallel lecture quotation. The classification can be taught without treating a chosen screen swatch as a universal human complexion or reading health and soul from actual people’s skin. Lecture 4’s drawing was materially limited. Note 22 at 149 c2 specifies the red-left/blue-right arrangement, radiating transitions, and unavailable colours. Keep the current teaching study’s original status explicit. The rainbow optics passage was only a set of hints with shorthand gaps. Note 38 at 150 c3 says this, then cites refraction and reflection within drops, including Steiner’s explanatory note. This qualification attaches to the earlier optical rainbow discussion; it is not a blanket statement that every line of Lecture 12 is missing. It supports careful source attribution and distinguishes an optical ray diagram from the spiritual rainbow sketches at 141–142. Plant colours and the Goetheanum are historically specified. Note 9 at 148 c1 and Note 36 at 150 c2 describe the cupola pigments/workshops. They do not authenticate the CSS hue choices as those pigments. No repository code or build output was modified during this review. No network calls or implementation-mirroring tests were used. The machine-readable companion is [private working file] .

title: Colour: frontmatter and core lecture capture ledger
text: Colour: frontmatter and core lecture capture ledger Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Current records / Registros atuais Current source record. Any explicitly dated historical sections remain historical, as the note explains. Registro atual de fontes. As seções históricas explicitamente datadas mantêm esse caráter, conforme explicado na nota. Page-by-page notes · English · 3474 words Contents of this note / Conteúdo desta nota Colour: frontmatter and core lecture capture ledger Colour: frontmatter and core lecture capture ledger This ledger records a full reading of Markdown captures 001–044 and visual comparison with every corresponding native PDF image. Capture 045 was also read and inspected to complete Lecture 3; its ledger row belongs to the next section of the review. These are reflowed, three-column PDF captures, not printed book folios. Columns are numbered left to right. A short capture, or a column left empty after a section ends, is not missing book text. The visible title page calls this Colour : three lectures given in Dornach on 6–8 May 1921, with nine supplementary lectures given on various occasions. Capture 003 explicitly assigns John Salter to lectures 1–3 and Pauline Wehrle to lectures 4–12, and records Translation © Rudolf Steiner Press 1992 . That is a translation copyright, not evidence of this file's publication year. The same capture says the first three lectures appeared as Colour in 1982, identifies the German title Das Wesen der Farben , GA 291, and gives ISBN 978 1 85584 275 5. It supplies no separately witnessed year of publication for this supplied edition. No author signature for the Foreword is visible in captures 005–009. The native boundaries are: Part One divider 014; Lecture 1, 015–023; Lecture 2, 024–033; Lecture 3, 034–045. The orientation reads the Foreword and synopses. Its short Steiner quotation previews Lecture 1, capture 015, column 3, and must not be attributed to the Foreword. Capture Essential source ideas and claims OCR/image comparison and visual evidence Essential teaching implication 001 Publisher's biographical portrait: anthroposophy as wisdom of the human being; spiritual perception, wide practical initiatives, books and lectures. Native image includes a small photographic portrait omitted by the text extraction. Prose agrees; OCR retains artificial word splits such as “devel- oped.” Columns 2–3 are mostly or wholly empty after the biography ends. Attribute the seer/science-of-spirit account to this biographical framing. It is not a lecture argument or an independently established account of spiritual perception. 002 Title, author, three Dornach lectures 6–8 May 1921 plus nine supplementary lectures; Salter and Wehrle named. Native title occupies column 1; Rudolf Steiner Press is at the top of column 2. OCR compresses “6 to 8.” No publication year appears. Teach the collection as a core course with later gathered talks, rather than twelve consecutive original lectures. 003 Salter translates 1–3; Wehrle 4–12. German title/GA 291; 1982 prior publication of first three; translation copyright 1992; ISBN. All metadata visually verified in columns 1–2. OCR merges some words and strips ISBN spacing; native reads “Translation © Rudolf Steiner Press 1992.” No edition publication year is printed here. Preserve translator provenance for every passage. Describe 1992 accurately as translation copyright, without inventing a publication date. 004 Contents separates Part One, Nature of Colour, from Part Two, supplementary lectures from other cycles, and names all twelve talks, References and Notes. Major OCR failure: most Part One titles/dates and many later headings disappear or become gibberish. Native three-column contents is complete and legible. Recover structure from the image; these are extraction omissions, not absent chapters or shorthand gaps. 005 Foreword presents colour as a forty-year strand in Steiner's work, beginning in Goethe studies; Goethe's organic science, 1884 morphology volume, Weimar period and colour edition. Quoted introduction defends a principle rather than every detail of Goethe's theory. OCR “Karl Julius Schroder” misreads native “Karl Julius Schröer”; “Kirschner” misreads “Kürschner.” Three-column chronology and long quotation are readable. Explain why the editor links art and scientific inquiry while retaining the qualification in Steiner's Goethe introduction. 006 Steiner never wrote the projected colour theory; lectures/sketches instead. Auric colour, Mystery Dramas and Johannes Thomasius lead to form as the work of colours; first Goetheanum cupolas and moral qualities of colour. Native places a verse passage with line breaks and a Ruth/Hans Pusch credit in column 2. OCR has spelling/line-wrap artifacts, including “Kiirschner”; no text gap is visible. Present painting out of colour as a developed artistic and spiritual ambition, not simply an improvised studio exercise. 007 Self-luminous spiritual figures require a different treatment from illuminated physical forms; naturalistic training caused difficulty. Steiner's cupola work, its destruction, teachers' physics courses, hoped-for experimental development and Research Institute closure. Text agrees after line-wrap normalization; three-column continuation is intact. The start completes the previous capture's sentence, not a missing opening. Explain the distinction between auric self-luminosity and ordinary cast light, and the Foreword's claim that scientific development should be tested by trained researchers. 008 Goethean art/science and metamorphosis; image/lustre distinctions across nature's kingdoms; how matter becomes coloured; alleged Sun/Moon creative forces; exercises and later lecture topics. Native has “Henni Geck,” where OCR reads “Henni Geek”; OCR also joins “in a.” No diagram is supplied on this capture. Give the actual spiritual answer proposed for material colour; retain art/science/metamorphosis as the Foreword's connecting argument. 009 Five late watercolours for eurythmy programmes show form arising through tone, movement and balance; reproductions available in the German complete edition. Text agrees. Only column 1 contains the short ending; columns 2–3 are empty. No reproduced painting appears here. Do not claim that the present capture includes those works or provides their colours; distinguish descriptions of artworks from visible reproductions. 010 Synopses of core lectures: feeling-based objective colour experience; four image colours; seven-colour cosmos, image/lustre, zodiac/planets; material colour and painting across kingdoms. Prose is readable; “8 may” in OCR is native “8 May.” No diagram is displayed. Use synopses as a route into the arguments, then read the lectures for the reasoning and qualifications. 011 Supplement synopses: flowing colour and human/animal consciousness, moral colour and tone, thought/light as past and will/darkness as future; nature/morality question begins. Text agrees; OCR joins “A world.” Capture starts with Lecture 3 synopsis continuation and ends mid-Lecture 7 synopsis. Preserve the chronological diversity and the actual spiritual arguments, including thought, will and reincarnation, when orienting later readings. 012 Synopses continue moral action's future world, colour/organism and treatment claims, Goethe versus Newton, colour perspective, Titian, beauty/ugliness and measure/number/weight. Native complete three-column prose confirms all topics. Hyphenated headings in OCR reflect wraps rather than missing phrases. Name medical and cosmological claims as claims; ordinary painting activities do not establish them. Make perspective/composition themes available without reducing the whole book to them. 013 Painting freed from weight; rainbow synopsis relates hierarchies and Saturn/Sun/Moon evolution, elemental beings and humanity as Fourth Hierarchy. Native ending occupies column 1; columns 2–3 empty. No rainbow illustration is present. Explain the final lecture's spiritual sequence, rather than equating its elemental beings with a physical explanation of rainbows. 014 Part One: Nature of Colour, basis for a spiritual-scientific understanding of colour for artists. Native section divider in column 1; empty remaining columns. OCR agrees. Treat this as a divider, not Lecture 1's opening or a blank/missing capture. 015 Lecture 1, 6 May 1921: art should speak to colour's objective nature; Goethe's nature/art aphorism; opposition to an ether-vibration account that leaves experienced colour behind. Feeling is to be permeated with insight. Native date/title and prose clear. Note 1 is a superscript in column 1; OCR flattens it. Orientation passage is exact in column 3. Explain Steiner's proposed objectivity within colour experience; merely recording personal reactions does not yet state his argument. Note 1 points to earlier physics courses. 016 Green with red, peach-blossom and blue figures: red enlivens green and demands motion; peach-blossom permits repose. These are comparative impressions, not finished pictures. Text agrees. No coloured patches or figures are drawn on this capture. Last word “es-” continues as “pecial” on 017. Label any course colour-field illustration as an application. State the author's actual felt results before inviting comparison. 017 Peach-blossom is neutral to green; blue dissipates greenness and imaginatively carries the meadow into an abyss. Colour experience needs imaginative comparisons; even physics uses analogy. Native continuous prose agrees. Initial “pecial” completes 016's “es-”; there is no missing phrase. Retain the strong contrast among animation, neutrality and dissipation, and explain why analogy is central to his method. 018 Plant life comes from its etheric body ; green belongs to physical/mineral appearance. Portraits illustrate image versus reality. Green is the lifeless image of the living; mineral, plant, animal and human differ by life/soul/spirit. Native prose and italic formula clear; OCR joins “such a.” No diagram yet. Explain image as one level presenting another, within the stated physical/ etheric account; a green patch is not itself the life it images. 019 Peach-blossom explicitly refers to human complexion, acknowledged to vary by person. Soul is said to reveal itself in complexion; greenish pallor and ruddy colour support the claimed living image of soul. Prose agrees after word-spacing normalization; native note 2 appears in column 3. The note body at 147 explicitly says this passage is incomplete in the transcript. That documented transcript gap is distinct from OCR damage. Represent the historical complexion claim accurately and examine its inference; do not use it to judge health, moral worth or identity. Do not silently insert the later 1923 repeat into the 1921 passage. 020 Blue cannot yet be reached through a characteristic natural being; white/light and black/darkness are approached through feeling. Light reveals colour but is not perceived like a coloured object's surface. Native “Newtonian fallacy” carries note 3 , column 3; OCR incorrectly prints 2. Otherwise prose agrees after wraps. Distinguish the experience of illumination from white pigment; note 3 explains the edition's Goethe/Newton polemic rather than settling modern optics. 021 Light and waking self-awareness connect the spiritual “I” with soul experience: white/light is soul's image of spirit. Black/carbon/diamond begins the fourth pairing. OCR sometimes reads “I” as “T”; native has “I.” Formula is in column 3. Carbon and diamond discussion is visibly part of the lecture. Give the self-awareness argument and its spiritual premise, without treating sight as a measure of personhood or carbon's colour as a complete physical account. 022 In blackness, life/soul cannot act but spirit can penetrate; black-white art is the example. Four formulas summarized; circle's preceding point supplies each adjective. Ascent black→green→peach-blossom→white mirrors lifeless→living→soul→spirit. Native four-line schema spans column 2; OCR loses separation. Passage ID 1 is exact in column 3. Diagram is referred to here but actually appears on 023. Teach the complete relational cycle, including black as spiritual image of lifelessness; avoid turning it into a list of arbitrary colour meanings. 023 Nature's coloured world is image rather than underlying reality. Green's imaging relation holds whether someone looks or not; that is Steiner's stated objectivity. Major diagram OCR noise. Native circular drawing in column 1: outer lifeless/top, living/right, soul/bottom, spirit/left; inner black/top, green/right, peach-blossom/bottom, white/left; between them four image formulas. Column 2 has the final argument; column 3 empty. Reconstruct the diagram's three related rings and direction. The claim of objectivity concerns the proposed relation in nature, not unanimous subjective reports. 024 Lecture 2, 7 May 1921: image formation through shadow-thrower and illuminant; spirit/lifeless→black, lifeless/living→green, living/soul→peach-blossom, soul/spirit→white. OCR flattens a real three-column table in native column 3. Table has headings Shadow-thrower / Illuminant / Image and four aligned rows. Keep the two inputs distinct. “Shadow” is a technical relational account, not an instruction to render all four colours as physically dark. 025 Green from yellow/blue acting on placid white; peach-blossom from interweaving black/white irradiated by red. The latter is an imagined process, said to operate in the organism; portraits only approximate it. Text agrees. Native contains no mixing diagram. Steiner explicitly says the imagined movement cannot be painted directly. Explain the opposed rest/movement processes, not a universal recipe for pigment or light mixing. 026 Green accepts boundaries; peach-blossom/lilac disperses as mood. Colour relationships are called amoral. Yellow demands a full centre fading outward, with boundaries alien to its nature. Native italic “Yellow must shine outwards” in column 3. Prose agrees; artificial OCR splits remain. State the strong artistic tendencies and the author's own amoral qualification; do not moralize people's taste or responses. 027 Blue shines inward from stronger circumference; Fra Angelico's even blue invokes divinity. Artists inhabit colour's demands, though artistic creation adds modifying factors. Red balances yellow/blue. OCR omits the actual three monochrome sketches in column 3: yellow dense centre fading out, red broadly even shading, blue dark rim/light centre. Native note 4 after Fra Angelico; OCR turns it into punctuation. Native really reads “a land of enclosure”; do not silently replace the edition's words. Explain distribution, not hue alone. Native diagrams support the comparison; retain the express qualification that artistic factors modify it. 028 Red acts through stillness and enduring surface; peach-blossom disperses/evaporates. Green and peach-blossom remain image-like, unlike inner radiance of lustres. Native italic red formula visible. Prose agrees; no new diagram. Distinguish red's inner movement at rest from peach-blossom's dissolution; both can look still without having the same function in the argument. 029 Images/shadows versus yellow, blue, red as outward expression of inner reality. Lustre radiates: outward yellow, inward blue, balanced red. Native two emphasized definitions in column 2. Existing passage ID 2 verified there, with line breaks normalized. OCR misreads one capital “I” as numeral 1 earlier. Define lustre as inner quality shining outward, not simply gloss. Preserve inward blue as a kind of radiance. 030 A straight physical spectrum is bent into a spiritual colour arrangement; peach-blossom above, green below; black/white interweave, warm/cold sides are lustres. Major diagram OCR noise. Native diagram in column 3: black/top; Image I/peach-blossom above; warm red/orange/yellow left as Lustre III; violet/indigo/blue right as Lustre IV; green/Image II below; white/bottom. Native prose has Roman III, where OCR can read “Ill.” Identify this as an expanded spiritual arrangement, not the ordinary physical spectrum or the four-image circle of 023. 031 Yellow lustre of spirit, blue of soul, red of living. Green after-image of red supports image/lustre pairing. Images compared with fixed zodiac pictures, lustres with moving planets; explicitly a comparison. Native formulas and text agree. No zodiac/planet illustration is present. Explain the three lustre formulas and the red/green reasoning. Do not turn the analogy into proof about celestial motion or physiology. 032 Artistic knowledge moves from feeling into practice. Even yellow must be given weight/mineralized as gold; early gold grounds give spirit an earthly dwelling. Colour mobility precedes colour fixed in objects. Native note 5 at Cimabue and 6 after “tomorrow,” both column 2; OCR misreads as 2 and ®. No gold-ground painting is reproduced. Explain the gold exception to radiating yellow. Note 6, across 147–148, preserves an additional Traub polemic about colour restricted to solid bodies; attribute it as editorial note content. 033 Colour descends to physical surfaces and raises the human being from material to spiritual. Short final paragraph in native column 1; remainder empty. OCR agrees. It completes Lecture 2's spiritual/artistic bridge; it is not a blank or a missing lecture ending. 034 Lecture 3, 8 May 1921: how does mobile colour become attached to matter? Goethe left this problem open; Steiner ridicules the selective absorption/reflection explanation as insufficient. Native note 7 , column 2, after Goethe's Theory of Colour ; OCR renders “?”. Prose/date/title intact. State the question and his criticism accurately while keeping the lecture's polemic distinct from present physical explanations of colour. 035 Green is the clearest fixed image colour. Occult Science supplies Old Moon fluid conditions and later Earth mineral incorporation, in which mobile plant colour becomes fixed green. Text agrees; no evolutionary diagram is shown. Old Moon is a prior Earth metamorphosis within Steiner's spiritual cosmology, not the present Moon's ordinary geological history. 036 Sunlight metamorphoses plant green into flower/fruit colours; Moon forces generate fixed green as image, analogous to Moon light reflecting Sun light. Cosmic image influences explain material fixation. Complete native prose agrees; no botanical colour plate or Sun/Moon diagram. Preserve the alleged Sun/Moon causal account as the author's answer, rather than reducing the passage to a generic observation of sunlight. 037 Separation of Moon from Earth explains green. Historical claim: landscape becomes possible in recent centuries because earlier painters treated all colour as image and lacked lustre treatment. Native note 8 after Titian in column 3; OCR prints 2. Names and main argument clear; no works reproduced. Explain how his history of painting depends on image/lustre. Present it as his historical interpretation, not an exhaustive art history. 038 Plants painted darker, then veiled in yellowish-white luminous atmosphere become living impressions. Lifeless furniture raises the problem of image-only copying versus painting. Prose agrees; OCR reads one “I” as 1. No landscape or furniture example is illustrated. Teach the specific plant process and its intended life effect; the author makes strong judgments about coloured furniture, not just neutral compositional suggestions. 039 Inorganic things require image colours transformed into inwardly shining lustres; a light source is imagined behind a transparent surface. Liquid paint pots are advocated over palette daubing. Native complete prose agrees. No palette or paint-pot illustration. Keep the conversion image→lustre central to painting lifeless things. Attribute the palette criticism to Steiner, while making the existing exercise an application rather than the proof. 040 Goetheanum plant colours facilitate inner luminosity. Minerals retain forces from planets formerly united with Earth, later expelled and acting externally; sunlight reveals but does not originate their intrinsic colour. Native note 9 in column 1 after “building”; OCR renders “?”. OCR also confuses “I”/“l” once. No mineral samples or planetary diagram. Give the actual planetary-force explanation. Note 9 adds plant-based laboratory colours used for both First Goetheanum cupolas. 041 Mineral colours linked to Mars/Mercury and Jupiter/Venus; inner light should be expressed behind the painted surface. Animals are painted lighter with pale blue shimmer, blending into plants' yellowish atmosphere. Native text agrees, all three columns complete; the final sentence continues on 042. Contrast mineral inner radiance, plant luminous veil and animal blue shimmer; do not lose the different treatments in a general instruction to “use washes.” 042 Fourfold table: mineral/lustre; plant/lustre-image; animal/image-lustre; human/image. Human painting converts lustre to image, approaching thought; colour boundaries modify yellow's ordinary demand. OCR flattens the aligned two-column table in native column 1 and merges “I am” as “lam” in column 3. Preserve the order of both compound terms. Explain why the human case deliberately changes a lustre's customary distribution. 043 Paint-pot liquid-to-solid practice recapitulates Old Moon/Earth colour evolution; joyful yellow, dignified red, tearful blue. Explicit rejection of symbolism meaning something other than colour itself. Goethe calls for artistic practical proof of colour laws. Text agrees apart from “I can” merged as “Ican.” No portrait/paint reproduction. Explain lived qualities rather than a symbol dictionary; the author advocates a spiritualized practice and criticizes lifeless palette portraits. 044 “I” and astral body live within colour outside physical embodiment, carrying it into physical/ etheric bodies . Subject/object separation is rejected. Dialogue with colour should guide its application; spiritual science continues on 045. Native note 10 in column 1; OCR wrongly gives 12. Several OCR “T” characters are native “I.” Existing passage ID 3 is exact in column 3. No illustration. Include the culminating embodiment claim, not only the convenient painting advice. Read 045 for the final claim that living Goetheanism must develop further through spiritual science. The four retained short passages are verified at 015/3, 022/3, 029/2 and 044/3 respectively. Their English wording is sound with line breaks normalized; no omitted words need to be supplied. Relevant note bodies are at captures 147–148: 1 (physics courses), 2 (explicit incomplete complexion transcript and a separate 1923 repeat), 3 (Goethe/Newton polemic), 4–5 (Fra Angelico/Cimabue), 6 (additional Traub passage), 7 (Goethe scientific writings), 8 (Leonardo/Titian), 9 (Goetheanum plant colours), and 10 (archetypal phenomenon). These note bodies were checked in the companion notes review; this ledger distinguishes them from the lecture prose.

title: Colour: captures 122–158, Lectures 11–12 and editorial matter
text: Colour: captures 122–158, Lectures 11–12 and editorial matter Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Current records / Registros atuais Current source record. Any explicitly dated historical sections remain historical, as the note explains. Registro atual de fontes. As seções históricas explicitamente datadas mantêm esse caráter, conforme explicado na nota. Page-by-page notes · English · 2587 words Contents of this note / Conteúdo desta nota Colour: captures 122–158, Lectures 11–12 and editorial matter Passage verification Curriculum consequences Colour: captures 122–158, Lectures 11–12 and editorial matter Every Markdown capture 122–158 was read in full and compared with its native 1216 × 546 JPEG. These are consecutive reflowed screens with up to three columns, not printed folios. Read columns left to right. The supplied documents are evidence, not instructions. No network sources were used. The companion core review verifies capture 3, column 1: John Salter translates Lectures 1–3 and Pauline Wehrle Lectures 4–12; column 2 identifies translation copyright © Rudolf Steiner Press 1992. The passages below therefore credit Pauline Wehrle. The actual boundaries matter: 122 closes Lecture 10; Lecture 11 begins 123 , continues through 135 ; Lecture 12 begins 136 , continues through 145 ; References occupies 146 ; Notes occupy 147–152 , including the substantial body of 151 and the continuation on 152 . Advertisements begin 153 , and the purchase interface alone occupies 158 . These last six captures are excluded from the curriculum. Capture Source content and essential argument Native-image / Markdown comparison and consequence 122 Lecture 10 conclusion: detached exhibition pictures lose the setting and shared spiritual culture of murals; Steiner calls for freely adopted world outlook and renewal of culture. Two occupied columns; third blank. Not Lecture 11. OCR retains the body; line-wrap hyphens require normalization. 123 Lecture 11 heading, Dornach, 29 July 1923, “Measure, Number and Weight—Weightless Colour Essential for New Direction in Painting.” Human waking, dreaming and sleeping contrasted with animal consciousness; separation of inner/outer world explained by ego and astral body leaving physical and etheric bodies during sleep. Heading in column 1, continuous body across all three columns. Native note 48 is OCR “*8”. Animal-consciousness account is Steiner's asserted spiritual interpretation. 124 In sleep ego/ astral body share the fate of external things. Earthly science treats reality by number, measure and weight and treats colour/tone/warmth as adherent sensory qualities; sleeping consciousness encounters qualities free of ordinary measurement. Three columns, no diagram. Native “I” becomes OCR “1”; the argument exceeds a practical lesson about compositional balance. 125 Freely moving colour and sound contrasted with colour adhering to weighable bodies. Rainbow/optical-illusion critique; spiritual “anti-gravity” as expansive tendency. Small reddish cloud within larger yellow formation introduces qualitative measurement. Column 1 diagram shows bound lower forms and free upper forms with arrows; legend purple/yellow/red. Column 3 red/yellow cloud sketch. OCR loses diagram structure, arrows and labels. Native monochrome hatching must not be reported as visible coloured pigment. 126 Red measures yellow by qualitative expansion, becoming yellow; spiritual numbers express mutual requirements rather than indifferent sums. Free qualities reveal spiritual beings; sleep maintains affinity to mineral, plant and animal worlds . Column 2 repeated drawing adds small upper circles to illustrate relation-dependent number; purple/yellow/red legend. OCR “RIS” and stray label fragments are diagram noise. Distinguish qualitative expansion from physical length measurement. 127 Capacity for sleep, rather than each successful night's sleep, grounds acknowledgement of outer world and truth. Dream forces become memory on re-entry into the body; artistic beauty shares dream's weaving of sympathy/antipathy, with a small “jolt” into bodily participation. Three columns, continuous text. Explicit insomnia qualification prevents changing the account into “sleepless people cannot know truth.” 128 Chaos is intermediate free weaving, freed from earthly weight but not yet dispersed; beauty arises by forming chaos into cosmos. Spiritual beings are determined by wisdom; goodness belongs to a being who may obey or refuse. Sleep→truth, dream→beauty/chaos, waking→goodness. Native table in column 3 has three aligned rows; OCR destroys the pairing. Native note 49, not OCR 42. Preserve exact row relationships and distinction between cosmic moral order and freely chosen goodness. 129 Steiner criticizes causal anthropology as describing a sleeper; waking activity requires goodness rather than truth alone. His polemic claims scientific habits encourage cultural sleep. No omitted illustration; all three columns occupied. Teach the argument as his criticism of reductionism, without converting it into an established statement that science cannot explain movement. 130 He acknowledges successful quantitative science but says qualities need recovery. Relativity and match/matchbox anecdote lead into limits of abstract relationships. Native note 50 appears in column 3; OCR 22. The historical criticism is subordinate to his attempt to recover qualitative experience. 131 Veal-cutlet example distinguishes directional real relations from exchangeable geometrical relations. The loss of qualitative colour/tone is linked to loss of art; artists turn toward Goethe. Earlier clairvoyant cultures valued qualities over quantities. Native note 51 remains attached to Einstein in column 1, not a stray folio. Polemical claims about relativity and physics are attributed. 132 Lavoisier and quantitative chemistry; ancient human being as microcosm. Gold in cosmic light said to form the heart; food treated as stimulus. Cimabue and Russian icons retain painting from the macrocosm. Native note 52, OCR “>2”. These are spiritual and historical assertions, not dietary or anatomical instructions. No heart diagram is present. 133 Gold background generates human form in antique art; Cimabue→Giotto→Raphael marks a move from cosmic icon to flesh with weight. Icons and Madonna paintings are contrasted; Renaissance light retains a fading glow of older gold. Small column 1 sketch between gold-background paragraph and Cimabue/Giotto transition is entirely absent from OCR. Note 53 is Giotto. Do not treat it as a reproduction of an identified icon. 134 Humanity “between two stools,” icon and Madonna: renewed art must experience free colour and paint out of colour consciously, rather than repeat old icons. Painted performance programmes exemplify the beginning. Closing critique of intellectualism/relativity/Hartmann. Exact retained quotation “We must learn to paint out of the colour.” is in column 1. Native notes 54 (programmes) and 55 (Hartmann), OCR *4/2?. 135 Lecture 11 final paragraph continues Hartmann/destructive-intellectualism polemic and calls for understanding impulses of the time. Only column 1 occupied; intentional short closing capture, not missing text and not Lecture 12. 136 Lecture 12 heading, Dornach, 4 January 1924, “The Hierarchies and the Nature of the Rainbow.” Introduction to modern spiritual research and reconstructed medieval thinking; chemical names and temperature-dependent states contrasted with real being. Three columns, note 56 in column 1 (OCR =°). Actual lecture start is 136. Steiner explicitly says he is not proceeding as a conventional historical chronology. 137 Cosmic intelligences gradually replaced by consciousness of earth/water/air/fire. Occult Science could have been expressed differently in earlier language. First Hierarchy: Seraphim's subject/object unity and enthusiasm. No diagram on this capture. Distinguish historical reconstruction from the later cosmic sequence. 138 Seraphim enthusiasm, Cherubim luminous thought, Thrones sustaining grace; concentric organization expresses differentiated warmth and Saturn existence. Warmth is manifestation of beings, not independently sufficient reality; beloved-person analogy. Column 2 Saturn diagram: Thrones kernel reddish-lilac, Cherubim yellow ring, Seraphim red outer covering, according to text. Native is monochrome; OCR drops all structural drawing evidence. 139 Second Hierarchy (Kyriotetes, Dynamis, Exusiai) enters First Hierarchy's warmth and manifests as light; densification produces air as light's shadow. Composition alone does not disclose a phenomenon's cosmic nature, illustrated by clock materials. Body spans three columns. Do not reduce “air is shadow of light” to modern gas chemistry or to an ordinary geometrical shadow. 140 Second Hierarchy's light/air gives Sun existence. Third Hierarchy (Archai, Archangels, Angels) brings longing and mediates light/darkness, giving colour. Aristotle cited; Newton criticized. Column 1 Sun diagram labels white rays, red background, green wavy marks. OCR substitutes meaningless fragments. Native note 57 points to Aristotle-related text. 141 Goethe/Newton polemic; water as reflection/creation of real cosmic colour. Red attacks/repels, blue/purple retreat and draw pursuit. Rainbow: elemental beings emerge around red/yellow and re-enter around green/blue, circulating as a spiritual cylinder. Column 2 rainbow bands labelled red/orange/yellow/green/blue/purple, with central upward arrow. OCR loses labels and drawing. Native note 58, not OCR 2®. 142 Emerging beings express fear, returning beings courage; 90-degree cross-section illustrates rainbow densification into water. Second Hierarchy/light and Third/colour summary; Moon existence. Fourth Hierarchy is original humanity before the Fall. Column 2 circular/cylindrical cross-section labelled Fear above, Courage below. Retained 27-word passage begins column 2 and ends column 3. Native note 59 is Albertus Magnus. 143 Fourth Hierarchy receives life: ego/ astral existence distinguished from etheric life. Life interpenetrates colour and forms edges/corners and solid crystal, giving Earth existence. Walking/sitting illustrate inner light/dark activity. Removing beings from nature compared with taking a person's clothes for the person. Three columns, no diagram until next capture. “Life” here has Steiner's technical etheric sense; do not infer that preceding spiritual beings were nonexistent. 144 Clothes-stand analogy critiques Kantian unknowable things and atomistic mechanism; spiritual science must put the person back in the clothes. Svedberg's modern-chemical reading of Basilius Valentinus is criticized as mistaking pictorial embryology for laboratory instructions. Column 2 tailor's dummy drawing omitted from OCR except noise. Native note 60 identifies Svedberg, note 61 Basilius; OCR 62/61. “Helmholzian” is the edition's spelling. 145 Lecture 12 ending: Wagner allusion and return to Christmas Foundation Meeting/world-history and human inner life. Short column 1 continuation. It contains neither References nor advertising. 146 References assigns supplementary lectures to GA volumes: 26 July 1914→286; 1 January 1915→275; 5/10 December 1920→202; 21 February 1923→349; 2/9 June 1923→276; 29 July 1923→228; 4 January 1924→233a. All dates/GA mappings visibly checked across three columns. These are edition mappings; the earlier review records the archive index's GA 286 classification for Lecture 5, but this cannot silently replace the supplied edition's GA 275. No new archive check was made. First three GA 291 lectures are verified in capture 3, column 1, by the core agent, not this supplementary list. OCR mangles German titles/diacritics, especially Brücke, Künstlerische, Mysterienstätten. 147 Notes introduction points to GA 291a. Notes 1–6: GA 320/321 science courses; incomplete peach-blossom passage and 1923 repeat; Newtonian/Goethean controversy; Fra Angelico; Cimabue; extra Traub polemic about colour tied to matter. Full body read, columns 1–3. Note 2 explicitly identifies transcript incompleteness; its historical “healthy skin” comparison is not a universal skin standard. Note 6 continues on 148. 148 Note 6 continuation; 7 Goethe GA 1 chapters XV–XVII; 8 Leonardo/Titian; 9 plant colours prepared for First Goetheanum cupolas; 10 archetypal phenomenon GA 1; 11 work here means First Goetheanum; 12 Grimm; 13 formerly Johannesbau; 14 Carstens; 15 Raphael; 16 Dante; 17 Homer. Full three-column body checked. These editorial identifications separate an obscure reference from an author claim; note 9 supplies provenance for pigment discussions. 149 Notes 18–29: Goethe on beauty/secret natural laws and Steiner's commentary; architectural references; animal-soul GA 56; 22 red-left/blue-right drawing and unavailable colours ; Hildebrand; July 1914 pre-war tension; art/Mystery cycle; Portal Scene 8; GA 202; Hegel/Schopenhauer; Galileo. Diagram erratum 22: red circle radiated red–orange–yellow into green, blue/purple other side, but Steiner lacked all colours and could not draw it properly. Note 29 continues on 150. Full three columns checked. 150 Notes 29–39: Galileo; December 1920 context/Rein; Boundaries of Natural Science; Waldorf GA 298; Philosophy of Freedom published 1893 with 1894 date; red/blue therapy reference; plant-colour laboratories/Anthea; Büttner's optics; 38 rainbow hints and shorthand gaps, refraction and reflection ; Arts and their Mission. Full body checked. Note 38 quotes Goethe calling rainbow complicated refraction with reflection and Steiner explaining raindrop passage/return to observer. This qualifies Lecture 8's incomplete treatment and prevents a simplistic light/dark account from replacing its admitted gaps. 151 Notes 40–55 : Steffen biography and 1921 colour report; supersensible-history lecture; GA 299 language; 2 June 1923 cross-reference; Kant quote; Goethe fairy tale; GA 271 arts talks; GA 225 Delegates' talks; chaos GA 284/285; previous-day GA 228; Einstein; Lavoisier; Giotto; 54 painted Goetheanum programmes since 1915, including Steiner's own ; Hartmann. Every column and note body checked, not skipped as advertising. Note 54 clarifies “programmes” in 134 as painted performance programmes; note 55 continues on 152. Table/pairings in 128 remain body argument rather than editorial inventions. 152 Notes 55 continuation and 56–61 : Hartmann; Christmas World History course; Aristotle-related short natural-science text and Goethe materials; Newton cross-reference; Albertus Magnus; Svedberg; Basilius Valentinus pseudonymous/alleged biography and publications. All body read and checked. Final note 61 ends in column 2; column 3 blank. Still editorial notes, excluded from no lesson's relevant evidence. Advertising boundary occurs only after this capture. 153 Publisher advertisement for Happiness, Rudolf Steiner, ISBN 9781855844919, 72 pages, description and purchase links. Cover and two “Buy now and read” links visible; promotional copy is not Colour's argument. Excluded from curriculum. 154 Publisher advertisement for Universe, Earth, Human Being, ISBN 9781855846401, 212 pages. Cover plus description/purchase links. Excluded from curriculum; its quoted mission of the age is not imported into this book. 155 Publisher advertisement for The Fall of the Spirits of Darkness, ISBN 9781855846388, 324 pages. Cover/promotional history and purchase links. Excluded from curriculum. 156 Publisher advertisement for Richard Masters's Rudolf Steiner and Social Reform, ISBN 9781855846326, 676 pages. Cover/author/book description/purchase links. Separate author, not Steiner lecture text. Excluded from curriculum. 157 Publisher advertisement for Results of Spiritual Research, ISBN 9781855846333, 416 pages. Cover/promotional description; purchase link continues to 158. Excluded from curriculum. 158 “Buy now and read” link only. Native image confirms otherwise blank screen. OCR's little-text warning does not mean omitted Colour content. Interface only; excluded from curriculum. Passage verification IDs 11 and 13: retain “We must learn to paint out of the colour.” (9 words), capture 134, column 1 . It follows the icon/Madonna comparison and calls for conscious renewal through weightless colour. A synthesis may apply the call only after reconstructing the source vocabulary and comparing supplementary arguments. ID 12: retain “In the course of the hierarchies entering into evolution the Second Hierarchy appeared in the form of light and the Third Hierarchy in the form of colour.” (27 words), capture 142, columns 2–3 . It begins at the bottom of column 2 and continues at the top of column 3; a single-column locator would be misleading. The following sentence gives Moon existence, and the preceding passage gives water as reflection of the hierarchies. Curriculum consequences Lecture 11 must teach the complete progression: waking/sleeping/dreaming; qualitative anti-gravity, colour-measure and dependent number; sleep/truth, dream/beauty, waking/goodness; formed chaos; quantitative science's achievement and asserted limits; icons/Cimabue, Giotto/Raphael/Madonna, and conscious renewal out of colour. A small-patch balancing exercise alone would replace its argument. Lecture 12 must name all three orders of beings and humanity as the Fourth Hierarchy; distinguish manifestation from reflection; preserve Saturn→warmth, Sun→light/air, Moon→colour/water, Earth→life/solid contours; include the rainbow's emergence/fear and return/courage, and explain the clothes-stand criticism of abstraction. These are attributed spiritual claims. Calling them simply an imaginative rainbow or a chemical recipe loses the lecture's intended explanation. Synthesis must first reconstruct image versus lustre and all seven formulas from the core text; next compare two supplementary lectures , with capture references and actual reasons/examples; only then produce the original portfolio. The draft offers Lecture 9 versus Lecture 11 as a worked comparison, while allowing other pairs from Lectures 4–12. Editorial clarifications are evidence; advertisements and purchase interface are not curriculum.

title: Colour: native-capture review, 045–088
text: Colour: native-capture review, 045–088 Original authored English; any bilingual material is retained as written. Inglês original do autor; os trechos bilíngues permanecem como foram escritos. Current records / Registros atuais Current source record. Any explicitly dated historical sections remain historical, as the note explains. Registro atual de fontes. As seções históricas explicitamente datadas mantêm esse caráter, conforme explicado na nota. Page-by-page notes · English · 30 September 2026 · 3244 words Contents of this note / Conteúdo desta nota Colour: native-capture review, 045–088 Existing lesson and passage comparison Colour: native-capture review, 045–088 Reviewed 30 September 2026. Every complete Markdown capture 045–088 was read and every corresponding native PDF image capture-NNN.jpeg was visually inspected. Capture 089 was additionally read and inspected to complete Lecture 7; its ledger row belongs to the adjoining review. These are 1216 × 546 three-column reflowed captures, not printed book folios. Columns run left to right. Blank columns at lecture endings are present in the PDF and do not establish missing text. The supplied file corrects the existing ranges: capture 045 concludes Lecture 3; 046 is the supplementary divider; Lecture 4 occupies 047–058, Lecture 5 occupies 059–069, Lecture 6 occupies 070–077, and Lecture 7 occupies 078–089. These four supplementary lectures are translated by Pauline Wehrle; 1992 is the translation copyright, not a verified publication date. The supplied References identify GA 286 for Lecture 4, GA 275 for Lecture 5 and GA 202 for Lectures 6–7. Editorial notes 146–151 were read for cross-reference only. Notes 22 and 24 explain the 1914 colour drawing and the imminent First World War; notes 30–34 identify the 1920 criticism and explain why Steiner gives 1893 for a first edition bearing the date 1894. Capture Essential argument and teaching implication Diagram / native layout Actual OCR–image comparison 045 Lecture 3 concludes that Goethe's approach must be developed into Steiner's spiritual science, including image and lustre. This is a methodological claim beyond Goethe, not the supplement introduction. Final paragraph in column 1; columns 2–3 blank. Prose agrees. No diagram or missing continuation is evidenced by the blank space. 046 Part Two announces supplementary lectures from other cycles. Teach the change of collection, chronology and context explicitly. Divider title in column 1; remaining area blank. Heading agrees; no lecture number or substantive teaching text is present. 047 Lecture 4, Dornach, 26 July 1914: Grimm's Goethe prediction introduces whole humanity and a reunion of cultural branches. Specialization in life separates people; the building's artistic form is meant to express unity. Title/date in column 1; three prose columns; no illustration. OCR corrupts superscript 11 as ?! and 12 as 22 . Native image clearly supplies the references. 048 Goetheanum colour is defended as outward expression of spiritual life. Carstens' drawing is contrasted with Raphael, Leonardo and Dante, whose themes allegedly lived in a shared culture. Teach this as Steiner's historical interpretation. Three prose columns; no artworks reproduced. Native footnotes 13–16 become !3 , 14 , 4® , 1® in OCR. These are reference errors, not missing accounts of the artworks. 049 Carstens' Homeric subjects exemplify the modern artist's isolation. Steiner contrasts questions about an artist's worldview with the aesthetic question of how a work is made when its subject is culturally shared. Three prose columns; no diagram. Superscript 17 after Iliad becomes punctuation. Line-wrap hyphenation requires normalization; the substantive argument is intact. 050 Art cannot arise directly from abstract scientific or theosophical concepts. Steiner opposes an ether-wave account to a living colour world and introduces animals' astral bodies and group souls. Preserve both the artistic criticism and its spiritual rationale. Three prose columns; no diagram. OCR misreads native references 18–20, including 8 , 2 and 22 . Scientific language here is the author's 1914 description. 051 Horses' alleged clairvoyance, the polar bear's whiteness and ancient Moon embodiment lead to humans' withdrawal from colour for ego development. Steiner's temperate-zone complexion generalization is a historical claim, not a rule for classifying people. Three prose columns; passage 4 appears in column 3.
